"Lithium-ion (Li-ion)",182.50,388.75,3.50,90,0.11435,"115-350","Assumptions (standardized for all technologies unless noted): discount rate = 8% (real); cycles_per_year = 300 (approx. daily cycling); depth-of-discharge (DoD) = 90%; usable_energy_per_cycle = DoD * round-trip-efficiency; median values for ranges taken as midpoint; CRF computed per reported median lifespan (Li-ion lifespan median = 12.5 years -> CRF ≈ 0.1295); opex values reported per kW-yr converted to per kWh-yr by dividing by median duration_hours; LCOC (levelized cost per kWh delivered) = (capex_kWh * CRF + opex_per_kWh_year) / (cycles_per_year * DoD * efficiency). For Li-ion: combined observations from BNEF (pack price $115/kWh — noted as pack/cell, not full installed) and PNNL (system-level 150–350 $/kWh; power-capex 300–450 $/kW). Where capex_per_kW missing we computed capex_per_kW = capex_per_kWh * median_duration_hours. Sensitivity (relative to median values): capex ±20% => LCOC = $0.1338 (+20%) / $0.0950 (-20%); duration ±50% => LCOC = $0.1087 (+50% duration) / $0.1315 (-50% duration). Notes: BNEF pack price understates installed system CAPEX; PNNL gives system-level ranges and reports LCOS typically $0.20–0.40/kWh (higher than our baseline because of different cycling/assumptions).","Sources used: BNEF (pack/cell pricing: $115/kWh, 2024) and PNNL (2022 system-level ranges: 150–350 $/kWh energy CAPEX; 300–450 $/kW power CAPEX; O&M and lifetime notes).","Numeric summary: Li-ion median capex = $182.50/kWh (median capex per kW = $388.75), median duration = 3.5 h, median round-trip efficiency = 90%. Using baseline assumptions (8% discount, 12.5 yr life, 300 cycles/yr, DoD 90%) median LCOC ≈ $0.114/kWh delivered. Sensitivity: +20% capex → $0.134/kWh; -20% capex → $0.095/kWh. +50% duration → $0.109/kWh; -50% duration → $0.132/kWh. BNEF pack price likely low-bound; use PNNL system-level numbers for more conservative planning."
"Supercapacitors / Ultra-capacitors",2000.00,300.00,0.15,89,1.47200,"1000-5000","Same baseline assumptions as above except lifespan median used = 25 years -> CRF ≈ 0.0937 for supercapacitors. Where source states '>>1000 $/kWh' I used a representative median = $2000/kWh and a plausible range 1,000–5,000 $/kWh (documented in notes). OPEX median taken as midpoint of reported ranges ($1–50/kW-yr -> $25/kW-yr) and converted to per-kWh-year by dividing by median duration_hours. LCOC calculation identical formula to Li-ion. Sensitivity (relative to median): capex ±20% => LCOC = $1.628 (+20%) / $1.317 (-20%); duration ±50% => LCOC = $1.242 (+50% duration) / $2.166 (-50% duration). Notes: supercapacitors are power-dense, extremely short-duration technologies; high $/kWh energy CAPEX and very short durations drive high delivered $/kWh costs even though cycle life is high. These median numbers are illustrative (sources describe 'very high' and '>>1000' $/kWh).","Sources used: Utility Dive summary of DOE materials (2023) and PNNL database entries (2022) noting very high system energy CAPEX for supercapacitors (>>$1000/kWh), short durations (sub-minute to minutes), high efficiency, and low typical energy capacity per project.","Numeric summary: Supercapacitors representative median capex = $2,000/kWh (range used 1,000–5,000), median capex per kW = $300, median duration ~0.15 h (~9 minutes), median efficiency ≈ 89%. Under baseline assumptions (8% discount, 25 yr life, 300 cycles/yr, DoD 90%) median LCOC ≈ $1.47/kWh delivered. Sensitivity: +20% capex → $1.63/kWh; -20% capex → $1.32/kWh. +50% duration → $1.24/kWh; -50% duration → $2.17/kWh. These values show supercapacitors are orders of magnitude more costly per delivered kWh than Li-ion for energy-shifting applications; they remain attractive only for ultra-short power services.
